videos.script: So far the programs that wrote to Kafka were small, and the ones that read were Kafka's own tools. In this lesson you write both. {{programs}} A producer looks simple. You hand it a message and it returns at once. But nothing has been sent yet. The message waits in a batch, and you only learn what became of it later, in a callback. {{batch}} A consumer reads in a loop. Run one copy and it reads every partition. Run three copies with the same group name, and Kafka shares the partitions out, one each. {{group}} Start a fourth, and it gets nothing at all. {{fourth}} Every time a copy joins or leaves, the partitions are dealt again. That is a rebalance, and there are three ways of doing it. {{rebalance}} And a consumer has to say how far it has read. Where it writes that down, and when, decides what a crash costs. {{commit}}
